units.title: Topic 1: The changing landscapes of the UK

topics.title: Overview of the UK's physical landscape

outcomes.text: Describe the distribution and characteristics of the UK's sedimentary, igneous and metamorphic rock types.
Explain how geology and past tectonic processes shaped upland (igneous, metamorphic) and lowland (sedimentary) landscapes.
Explain how upland and lowland landscapes result from glacial, weathering, river and slope processes working together.
Explain how agriculture, forestry and settlement have shaped landscapes over time.

topics.title: Optional sub topic 1A: Coastal landscapes and processes

outcomes.text: Describe coastal weathering, mass movement, erosion, transport (including longshore drift) and deposition.
Explain how geological structure, rock hardness and wave type influence coastal landforms.
Explain how UK weather and climate affect rates of coastal erosion and retreat.
Explain how erosion forms headlands, bays, caves, arches, stacks, cliffs and wave cut platforms.
Explain how deposition forms bars, beaches and spits.
Explain how human activity affects coasts and how coastal recession and flooding affect people and the environment.
Evaluate hard and soft coastal defences (sea walls, groynes, rip rap, beach nourishment, managed retreat).
Explain the location, formation and main factors of change of one named UK coastal landscape.

topics.title: Optional sub topic 1B: River landscapes and processes

outcomes.text: Describe river weathering, mass movement, erosion, transport and deposition.
Explain how channel shape, valley profile, gradient, discharge, velocity and sediment change along a named UK river.
Explain how UK weather events and climate affect river processes and landforms.
Explain how erosion and geology form interlocking spurs, waterfalls, gorges and river cliffs.
Explain how deposition forms flood plains, levees and point bars.
Explain how erosion and deposition together form meanders and oxbow lakes.
Explain how land use change affects river processes and the causes and effects of flooding.
Evaluate hard (dams, reservoirs, channelisation) and soft (flood plain zoning, washlands) river defences.
Explain the location, formation and main factors of change of one named UK river landscape.

topics.title: Optional sub topic 1C: Glaciated upland landscapes and processes

outcomes.text: Describe the glacial erosion, transport and deposition that once shaped upland landscapes.
Describe the freeze-thaw, soil movement and rock fall processes acting on glaciated landscapes today.
Explain how past climate and current UK weather affect processes in glaciated uplands.
Explain how erosion forms truncated spurs, corries, troughs, tarns, arêtes, hanging valleys and roche moutonnées.
Explain how deposition forms ground and terminal moraines.
Explain how erosion and deposition together form crag and tails and drumlins.
Explain how farming, forestry and settlement affect physical processes in glaciated uplands.
Evaluate development such as water supply, renewable energy, tourism and conservation in glaciated uplands.
Explain the location, formation and main factors of change of one named UK glaciated upland.

units.title: Topic 2: Weather hazards and climate change

topics.title: Global atmosphere and climate change

outcomes.text: Describe the features of global atmospheric circulation.
Explain how circulation cells and ocean currents redistribute heat around the Earth.
Describe how climate changed over Quaternary glacial and interglacial periods.
Explain natural causes (Milankovitch cycles, solar variation, volcanism) and the evidence (ice cores, pollen, tree rings, records) for climate change.
Explain how industry, transport, energy and farming produce greenhouse gases that enhance the greenhouse effect.
Describe effects of climate change on environment and people: crop yields, sea level rise and retreating glaciers.
Describe the UK's climate today and how it has changed over 1000 years.
Describe spatial variations in UK temperature, wind and rainfall.
Explain how the UK's geographic location influences its climate.

topics.title: Tropical cyclones

outcomes.text: Explain how global circulation produces tropical cyclones and the sequence of their formation.
Describe the characteristics, frequency and distribution of tropical cyclones and how they change over time.

subtopics.title: Impacts of and responses to tropical cyclones

outcomes.text: Explain why tropical cyclones are hazards: winds, rainfall, storm surges, flooding and landslides.
Compare social, economic and environmental impacts of tropical cyclones in a named developed and a named developing or emerging country.
Compare responses of individuals, organisations and governments to tropical cyclones in those two countries.

topics.title: Drought

outcomes.text: Contrast the characteristics of arid environments with drought conditions.
Explain meteorological, hydrological and human causes of drought.
Explain why global circulation makes some places more vulnerable to drought and how this changes over time.

subtopics.title: Impacts of and responses to drought

outcomes.text: Explain why droughts are hazardous.
Compare drought impacts on people and ecosystems in a named developed and a named developing or emerging country.
Compare responses to drought by individuals, organisations and governments in those two countries.

topics.title: Global and UK ecosystems

outcomes.text: Describe the distribution and characteristics of the world's large-scale ecosystems.
Explain how climate, soils and altitude influence where ecosystems are found.
Explain how the biosphere supplies food, medicine, materials and fuel and is increasingly exploited for energy, water and minerals.
Describe the distribution and characteristics of UK moorlands, heaths, woodlands and wetlands.
Explain the importance of marine ecosystems to the UK and how human activity degrades them.

topics.title: Tropical rainforests

outcomes.text: Describe the biotic and abiotic characteristics of the tropical rainforest.
Explain the interdependence of these characteristics and the nutrient cycle (Gersmehl model).
Explain why rainforests have high biodiversity and how plants and animals are adapted.
Give examples of goods and services from tropical rainforests.
Explain how climate change threatens rainforest structure, function and biodiversity.
Explain the economic and social causes of deforestation.
Explain the political and economic factors in sustainable management of a rainforest in a named region.

topics.title: Deciduous woodlands

outcomes.text: Describe the abiotic and biotic characteristics of the deciduous woodland ecosystem.
Explain the interdependence of these characteristics and the nutrient cycle (Gersmehl model).
Explain why deciduous woodlands have moderate biodiversity and how plants and animals are adapted.
Give examples of goods and services from deciduous woodlands.
Explain how climate change threatens deciduous woodland structure, function and biodiversity.
Explain the economic and social causes of woodland deforestation.
Describe approaches to sustainable use and management of deciduous woodland in a named region.

topics.title: Overview of urban patterns and processes

outcomes.text: Compare urbanisation trends over 50 years in developed, emerging and developing countries.
Explain how and why urbanisation happened at different times and rates around the world and its effects.
Describe the distribution of UK urban population and its major urban centres.
Explain the factors causing the rate and degree of urbanisation to differ between UK regions.

topics.title: Case study of a major UK city

outcomes.text: Explain the site, situation and connectivity of the chosen UK city in national, regional and global context.
Describe the chosen city's structure (CBD, inner city, suburbs, urban-rural fringe) by function and building age.
Describe urbanisation, suburbanisation, counter-urbanisation and re-urbanisation in the chosen UK city.
Explain the causes of migration and its impact on different parts of the chosen UK city.
Use Census data to describe the city's population and explain its growth or decline.
Explain the causes and impacts of deindustrialisation in the chosen UK city.
Explain how economic change increases inequality and differences in quality of life.
Explain how changes in retailing affect the city: CBD decline, out-of-town centres and internet shopping.
Describe strategies for making urban living more sustainable and improving quality of life.

topics.title: Case study of a major city in a developing or emerging country

outcomes.text: Explain the site, situation and connectivity of the chosen city in national, regional and global context.
Describe the chosen city's structure by function and building age.
Explain past and present population growth trends: natural increase, migration and investment.
Explain the causes of migration and its impact on different parts of the chosen city.
Explain how growth brings inequality and differences in quality of life.
Describe challenges of rapid urbanisation: infrastructure, services, housing, informal employment and pollution.
Evaluate bottom-up and top-down approaches to managing the city's challenges.
Explain the role of government policies in improving quality of life in the city.

topics.title: Overview of global development

outcomes.text: Compare economic and broader social and political ways of defining development.
Explain the economic, social, technological and cultural factors, and food and water security, that contribute to development.
Describe how development is measured: GDP per capita, Human Development Index, inequality measures and corruption indices.
Describe the global pattern of development and its unevenness between and within countries, including the UK.
Explain the physical, historic and economic factors behind spatial variations in development.
Explain how uneven development affects quality of life: housing, health, education, jobs, technology, food and water security.
Describe international aid and inter-governmental agreements that try to reduce uneven development.
Compare top-down and bottom-up development projects, with their advantages and limitations.

topics.title: Case study of a developing or emerging country

outcomes.text: Describe the chosen country's location and position in its region and globally.
Describe its political, social, cultural and environmental context.
Explain the unevenness of development within the country (core and periphery) and why it varies.
Evaluate positive and negative impacts of change in the primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors.
Describe the country's international trade and aid.
Explain the changing balance between public and private investment.
Describe changes in population structure and life expectancy over 30 years.
Describe changing social factors: inequality, a growing middle class and better education.
Explain how geopolitical relationships affect the country's development.
Explain how technology and connectivity support development for different areas and groups.
Evaluate the positive and negative social, economic and environmental impacts of rapid development.
Explain how the government and people manage these impacts to improve quality of life and global status.

topics.title: Overview of the global and UK distribution of food, energy and water

outcomes.text: Define and classify natural resources as biotic, abiotic, renewable and non-renewable.
Describe how people exploit environments for water, food and energy.
Explain how exploitation changes environments: biodiversity loss, soil erosion, poorer water and air quality.
Describe the global and UK distribution of soil, forestry, fossil fuels, water, rock and minerals.
Describe global patterns of use and consumption of food, energy and water.

topics.title: Optional sub topic 6A: Energy resource management

outcomes.text: Classify energy resources as renewable or non-renewable.
Evaluate production of one non-renewable energy resource.
Evaluate production of one renewable energy resource.
Describe the composition of the UK's energy mix.
Explain how population, wealth and resource availability shape energy mixes worldwide.
Explain how global energy demand and supply changed over 100 years through population growth, wealth and technology.
Evaluate impacts on people and environment of developing coal, oil, gas and uranium.
Evaluate impacts of developing hydro-electric, wind and solar power.
Explain how fracking can resolve energy shortages.
Explain how attitudes to energy exploitation and consumption differ among individuals, organisations and governments.
Explain why renewable and non-renewable energy need sustainable management.
Compare views of individuals, organisations and governments on sustainable energy use.
Describe how one developed and one emerging or developing country manage energy sustainably.

topics.title: Optional sub topic 6B: Water resource management

outcomes.text: Describe the global distribution of fresh water.
Explain how water availability varies at global, national and local scales.
Explain why some places have a water surplus or deficit.
Explain how human intervention changed water supply and demand over 50 years.
Compare use of water by agriculture, industry and households in developed and developing countries.
Explain why water use differs between developed and developing countries.
Explain why the UK has water supply problems: imbalances, seasonal gaps and ageing pipes.
Explain why emerging and developing countries have water supply problems.
Explain how attitudes to water exploitation differ among stakeholders.
Explain how desalination can resolve water shortages.
Explain why water resources need sustainable management.
Compare views of individuals, organisations and governments on sustainable water use.
Describe how one developed and one emerging or developing country manage water sustainably.

topics.title: 7A: Investigating physical environments

outcomes.text: Develop investigable questions about change in a river channel based on the location and task.
Use a quantitative method to measure river discharge and a qualitative method to record river landforms.
Explain the implications of river processes for people living in the catchment.
Use a flood risk map and one other secondary source.
Develop investigable questions about coastal processes using landscape evidence.
Use a quantitative method to measure beach morphology and sediment, and a qualitative method to record coastal landforms.
Explain the implications of coastal processes for people living on the coast.
Use a geology map and one other secondary source.

topics.title: 7B: Investigating human environments

outcomes.text: Develop investigable questions about change in a central or inner urban area.
Record the quality of the urban environment qualitatively and measure land use function quantitatively.
Explain how physical landscape features interact with the urban area, residents and visitors.
Use Census data and one other secondary source.
Develop investigable questions about change in rural settlements.
Record people's views on rural environmental quality and measure flows of people in a settlement.
Explain how physical landscape features interact with rural settlements, residents and visitors.
Use Census data and one other secondary source.

topics.title: The fieldwork enquiry process

outcomes.text: Explain the kinds of question fieldwork can investigate and the enquiry process used.
Explain the range of fieldwork techniques and methods, including observation and measurement.
Process and present fieldwork data using maps, GIS, graphs and diagrams.
Analyse and explain fieldwork data using relevant case studies and theories.
Draw evidenced conclusions from fieldwork data.
Reflect critically on fieldwork data, methods, conclusions and knowledge gained.

topics.title: The four UK challenges

outcomes.text: Explain how UK population change over 50 years affects resource consumption.
Explain the pressures of growing populations on UK ecosystems.
Describe national sustainable transport options for the UK.
Explain the two-speed economy and options for bridging the gap between the south east and the rest of the UK.
Weigh the costs and benefits of greenfield development against brownfield regeneration.
Evaluate UK net migration statistics and the differing attitudes of stakeholders to migration.
Describe approaches to conserving and developing UK National Parks.
Describe approaches to managing river and coastal flood risk in the UK.
Explain the uncertainties about how global climate change will affect the UK's future climate.
Describe the impacts of climate change on people and landscapes in the UK.
Describe local and national responses to climate change in the UK.
